ITEM.PTXT: A non-contact type accelerator position sensor has been adopted, using a Hall element that can extract the magnetic field strength as an electrical signal using the Hall effect, which provides an output voltage linear to the accelerator pedal depression amount. When the accelerator pedal depression amount changes, the angle of the magnetic field relative to the flow of the applied current in the Hall element changes, so the strength of the magnetic field perpendicular to the applied current changes. The resulting change in voltage, generated perpendicular to both the applied current and the magnetic field, is sent to the engine control computer as the accelerator pedal depression amount signal. In addition, reliability is ensured by adopting a 2-system (main and sub) sensor with different output characteristics.

This is a phenomenon in which, when a current flows through a rod- or plate-shaped conductor or semiconductor and a magnetic field is applied perpendicular to it, a potential difference is generated in the direction perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field.
This is an electronic component that uses the electromotive force generated by the potential difference in a magnetic field.
The accelerator position sensor detects the opening angle with 2 systems: a main circuit and a sub circuit. If a malfunction occurs in the signal, the engine control computer switches to limp mode.

ENTRY.PTXT: If a malfunction occurs in either circuit, the engine control computer detects the malfunction from the voltage difference between the main circuit and sub circuit. At this time, a limited accelerator opening angle is calculated from the sensor value of 2 circuit, and throttle control is continued, enabling limp mode driving.
The engine control computer detects the malfunction from the voltages of the main circuit and sub circuit and controls the throttle valve opening angle only within the idling range.
